questions.stem: A man spends 75% of his income. If his income is Rs. 24,000, how much does he save?
What is 25% of 480?
A number is increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net effect?
questions.keySolution: Let original number = 100 - After 20% increase = 100 + 20 = 120 - After 20% decrease = 120 - (20/100 × 120) = 120 - 24 = 96 - Net change = 96 - 100 = -4% (4% decrease)

questions.stem: In a class, 60% are boys and the rest are girls. If there are 30 girls, what is the total strength of the class?
questions.keySolution: Girls = 40% of total class (since boys = 60%) - 40% of total = 30 - Total = 30 × (100/40) = 75

questions.stem: A student scored 480 marks out of 600. What is the percentage?
The price of a shirt is increased by 20% and then decreased by 25%. What is the net change in price?
questions.keySolution: Let original price = 100 - After 20% increase = 100 + 20 = 120 - After 25% decrease = 120 - (25/100 × 120) = 120 - 30 = 90 - Net change = 90 - 100 = -10 (10% decrease)

questions.stem: 30% of a number is 270. What is the number?
If A’s salary is 20% more than B’s, then how much percent is B’s salary less than A’s?
questions.keySolution: Let B’s salary = 100 - A’s salary = 120 (20% more) - B’s salary is less than A’s by = (120-100)/120 × 100 = 20/120 × 100 = 16.66%

questions.stem: A number is first increased by 10% and then decreased by 10%. What is the net effect?
questions.keySolution: Let original number = 100 - After 10% increase = 110 - After 10% decrease = 110 - (10/100 × 110) = 110 - 11 = 99 - Net change = 99 - 100 = -1% (1% decrease)

questions.stem: If 60% of a number is 150, then what is the number?
A shopkeeper gives a discount of 20% and still makes a profit of 20%. The cost price of an item is Rs. 400. What is its marked price?
questions.keySolution: Cost Price = Rs. 400 - Selling Price = 400 + 20% of 400 = 400 + 80 = Rs. 480 - Marked Price with 20% discount = Selling Price - MP - 20% of MP = 480 - 80% of MP = 480 - MP = 480 × (100/80) = Rs. 600

questions.stem: If the price of sugar is increased by 25%, by what percentage should a household reduce its consumption so as not to increase its expenditure?
questions.keySolution: Let original consumption = 100, original price = 1, expenditure = 100 - New price = 1.25 - To keep expenditure same = 100, consumption = 100/1.25 = 80 - Reduction = (100-80)/100 × 100 = 20%

questions.stem: A salary is increased by 10% and then decreased by 10%. What is the effective percentage change?
questions.keySolution: Same as Q9: 1% decrease - Let original salary = 100 - After 10% increase = 110 - After 10% decrease = 99 - Net = -1% (1% decrease)

questions.stem: If 20% of a is equal to 30% of b, then a:b is?
A man spends 85% of his income. If he saves Rs. 750, what is his income?
questions.keySolution: Spends 85%, saves 15% - Savings = Rs. 750 - Income = 750 × (100/15) = Rs. 5,000

questions.stem: In an exam, a student scored 30% and failed by 30 marks. Another student scored 40% and got 30 marks more than the pass mark. What is the maximum mark?
questions.keySolution: Let maximum marks = x - Student A: 30% of x = pass marks - 30 - Student C: 65% of x = pass marks + 30 - From A: Pass marks = 0.3x + 30 - From C: Pass marks = 0.65x - 30 - 0.3x + 30 = 0.65x - 30 - 60 = 0.35x - x = 600

questions.stem: The population of a town increased by 20% in a year and then decreased by 20% in the next year. What is the net change?
questions.keySolution: Let original population = 100 - After 20% increase = 120 - After 20% decrease = 120 - (20/100 × 120) = 96 - Net change = 96 - 100 = -4% (4% decrease)

questions.stem: A man gives 10% of his salary to his wife, 20% of the rest to his son. If he is left with Rs. 7,200, what was his salary?
questions.keySolution: Gives 10% to wife: 90% remains - Gives 20% of 90% to son: 0.2 × 90 = 18% of total - Left with: 100 - 10 - 18 = 72% = Rs. 7,200 - Total salary = 7,200 × (100/72) = Rs. 10,000 -

questions.stem: If A’s salary is 25% more than B’s, then B’s salary is how much percent less than A’s?
questions.keySolution: Let B’s salary = 100 - A’s salary = 125 (25% more) - B is less than A by = (125-100)/125 × 100 = 25/125 × 100 = 20%

questions.stem: If the price of petrol increases by 20%, by how much percent must a car owner reduce consumption to keep the same budget?
questions.keySolution: Same calculation as Q12: 16.66% reduction needed

questions.stem: A man spends 30% of his income on rent, 20% on food, and 10% on transport. If his income is Rs. 10,000, how much does he save?
questions.keySolution: Income = Rs. 10,000 - Rent = 30% = Rs. 3,000 - Food = 20% = Rs. 2,000 - Transport = 10% = Rs. 1,000 - Total spent = Rs. 6,000 - Savings = 10,000 - 6,000 = Rs. 4,000

questions.stem: If the passing marks in an exam are 40% and a student scores 180 marks and fails by 20 marks, what are the maximum marks?
questions.keySolution: Student fails by 20 marks, so pass marks = 180 + 20 = 200 - Pass marks are 40% of total - 40% of total = 200 - Total marks = 200 × (100/40) = 500

questions.stem: A product is sold at a 20% profit. If the cost price is Rs. 500, what is the selling price?
questions.keySolution: Cost Price = Rs. 500 - Selling Price = 500 + 20% of 500 = 500 + 100 = Rs. 600

questions.stem: If x is 40% of y and y is 60% of z, then x is what percent of z?
A’s income is 25% more than B’s income. By what percent is B’s income less than A’s?
questions.keySolution: Same as Q19: B is 20% less than A

questions.stem: A number is increased by 15% and the result is 460. What was the original number?
questions.keySolution: Original number increased by 15% = 460 - Original number = 460 × (100/115) = 400

questions.stem: If 75% of a number is 300, what is the number?
If 10% of a number is 25, what is the number?
The price of an item is increased by 10%. Then it is decreased by 10%. What is the net effect?
questions.keySolution: Same as Q9: 1% decrease

questions.stem: A man earns Rs. 6,000 per month. He saves 20%. What is his expenditure?
questions.keySolution: Income = Rs. 6,000 - Saves 20% = Rs. 1,200 - Expenditure = 6,000 - 1,200 = Rs. 4,800

questions.stem: The price of an article is increased by 40% and then decreased by 30%. What is the net change?
questions.keySolution: Let original price = 100 - After 40% increase = 140 - After 30% decrease = 140 - (30/100 × 140) = 140 - 42 = 98

questions.stem: A man’s salary was increased by 10% and then decreased by 10%. What is the net effect?
questions.keySolution: Same as Q13: 1% decrease

questions.stem: If a number is 20% more than another, what percent is the second less than the first?
questions.keySolution: let first = 120, second = 100 - Then 100 is less by 20/120 = 16.66%

questions.stem: A person spends 75% of his income. If his income increases by 20% and his expenditure increases by 10%, what is the percentage increase in savings?
questions.keySolution: Let original income = 100, spending = 75, savings = 25 - New income = 120 (20% increase) - New spending = 75 × 1.1 = 82.5 (10% increase) - New savings = 120 - 82.5 = 37.5 - Increase in savings = (37.5 - 25)/25 × 100 = 12.5/25 × 100 = 50%

questions.stem: A quantity is increased by 50% and then decreased by 50%. What is the net change?
questions.keySolution: Let original quantity = 100 - After 50% increase = 150 - After 50% decrease = 150 - (50/100 × 150) = 150 - 75 = 75 - Net change = 75 - 100 = -25% (25% decrease)

questions.stem: A number when decreased by 20% gives 80. What is the original number?
questions.keySolution: Number decreased by 20% = 80 - Original = 80 × (100/80) = 100

questions.stem: The difference between 63% of a number and 45% of the same number is 342. What is the number?
questions.keySolution: 63% of number - 45% of number = 342 - 18% of number = 342 - Number = 342 × (100/18) = 1,900

questions.stem: If the population of a town increases by 10% annually, what will be the population after 2 years if the current population is 10,000?
questions.keySolution: Current population = 10,000 - After 1 year = 10,000 × 1.1 = 11,000 - After 2 years = 11,000 × 1.1 = 12,100

questions.stem: A man spends 40% on food, 30% on rent, and 20% on other expenses. If he saves Rs. 900, what is his monthly income?
What percentage of 80 is 40?
If the price of a commodity is reduced by 25%, what percentage increase is needed to restore the original price?
questions.keySolution: Reduced by 25%, so now = 75% of original - To restore, need increase of 25/(75) × 100 = 33.33%

questions.stem: In a group, 45% are male and 55% are female. If there are 220 females, how many males are in the group?
A man’s income is increased by 15% and then decreased by 5%. What is the net change in his income?
questions.keySolution: Let original income = 100 - After 15% increase = 115 - After 5% decrease = 115 - (5/100 × 115) = 115 - 5.75 = 109.25 - Net change = 9.25%

questions.stem: The difference between 80% of a number and 60% of the same number is 50. Find the number.
questions.keySolution: 80% of number - 60% of number = 50 - 20% of number = 50 - Number = 50 × (100/20) = 250

The percentage increase from 200 to 300 is?
If a number is decreased by 15%, the result is 170. What is the original number?
questions.keySolution: Number decreased by 15% = 170 - Original = 170 × (100/85) = 200

questions.stem: A student answered 85% of the questions correctly. If he answered 51 questions correctly, how many total questions were there?
The price of a house increased by 20% one year and decreased by 10% the next year. If the original price was Rs. 5,00,000, what is the price after 2 years?
questions.keySolution: Original price = Rs. 5,00,000 - After 20% increase = 5,00,000 × 1.2 = Rs. 6,00,000 - After 10% decrease = 6,00,000 × 0.9 = Rs. 5,40,000
